title: Incremental ABI guardrails and rollback helpers for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Recent dependency upgrades across CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS introduced intermittent kernel ABI mismatches and non-deterministic perf regressions in tail latency. Several large refactors have landed (see related issues) but we lack an incremental validation + safe-rollback path that teams can use when updating driver/runtime or kernels. This ticket implements a small, reusable guardrail system and developer helpers to make future dependency upgrades lower risk.

Goals:
- Provide automated ABI compatibility checks for our kernel bundles against target CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS versions.
- Add microbench-based fingerprinting to detect small perf regressions before a full rollout.
- Create a rollout policy helper that can: pin kernel adapters, perform canary with KV-cache warmup, and automatically trigger graceful rollback on prespecified signals (error spike, latency P95 breach, or token cost jump).
- Surface quick triage artifacts (per-commit perf diffs, kernel symbol map) in the Console deployment page and link to a PR template.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: build validation CI jobs, a lightweight local dev script, a canary+rollback orchestration helper, and Console links for triage. Implementations will be added to the runtime repo and infra pipelines.
- Non-goal: full upstream CUTLASS refactor or major runtime re-architecture (those are separate initiatives). This is risk-reduction plumbing to make upgrades safer and faster.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job 'gpu-abi-check' runs on branch builds and produces a human-readable compatibility report (symbols missing/changed, size deltas).
- 'microbench-fingerprint' job runs a 30s kernel microbench across curated shapes and reports a deltas summary; regressions flagged if median latency increases >10% or P95 >15%.
- Canary helper runbook + automated script exists: canary-config.yaml schema, CLI to launch canary with traffic split, and an automatic rollback trigger based on Console webhook.
- Documentation: PR template, console triage links, and a short how-to for engineers performing dependency upgrades.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design compatibility report schema (symbols, versions, diff score).
2) Implement lightweight symbol extractor in runtime repo (hermetic, no GPUs required).
3) Add CI jobs that consume built artifacts and compare against baseline builds stored in S3/artifacts bucket.
4) Wire microbench harness that runs a curated set of shapes on target hardware in a fenced test pool. Publish perf fingerprints.
5) Build canary CLI that configures route split + KV-cache warmup + metrics hooks; implement simple rollback orchestrator using existing routing policy framework.
6) Add Console links and PR template to surface reports automatically.

Risks and mitigations:
- Flaky microbench results due to noisy infra: mitigate with repeated runs and statistical smoothing, and place canaries on isolated infra.
- False positives for ABI diffs (benign symbol renames): include heuristics and allow ignore lists per kernel family.
- Rollback causing transient errors: implement graceful fallback (keep old variant active until new variant fully marked unhealthy).

Related work and dependencies:
- ENG-7359 (gpu stack modernization) - informational; existing kernel ABI changes reference.
- ENG-12846 (scheduler interface consolidation) - potential dependency for rollout orchestration.
- ENG-27311 (runtime kernel fallback) - consume fallback primitives here.
- infra/ops ticket(s) to provision fenced test pool for microbench runs (TBD).

Release target: runtime-1.19 (guardrail features gated behind feature flag).

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the compatibility report schema and the microbench shapes. The CLI and Console links are intentionally minimal MVPs.
- Security: no customer data should be included in CI artifacts; ensure we scrub any sample prompts that might be captured in traces.

2026-03-08 QA: Microbench harness runs but results noisy on shared CI GPU. Suggest using a dedicated test pool and increasing run count to 5 per shape.
2026-03-10 PM (Rina Patel): Requested that Console triage links include direct link to PR and the failing perf graph; added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez: Canary CLI MVP implemented; manual canary executed on test pool (small traffic split). Observed P95 spike in one kernel shape; rollback triggered and traffic restored to baseline. Documenting the run in Drive.
